preview: Goldman Sachs interview experience for a Summer Analyst internship by Dhrumil Raigagla, detailing the online test and three technical rounds.
content: Goldman Sachs Interview Experience for Internship as a Summer Analyst. DHRUMIL RAIGAGLA, I.T. 2020-2024. 13-08-2022 - Online Test. Students from all branches were allowed to sit for the test. The test was on Hackerrank and was divided into four sections. It was a proctored test that required camera and audio permissions. Changing the tab would lead to being flagged. Each section had a separate timer which meant that you could not carry forward the time from any other section and you couldn’t navigate back to a section after submitting it. 4 Sections of Online test: (1) Coding/Programming Questions: (30 mins). There were 2 coding questions of moderate difficulty. Maximum sum square sub-matrix of given size (similar question here). The question was not direct, a long story was given. There is a football player who wants to score a goal in square sub-region of a ground. The ground is represented by a n*n 2-d matrix where each element is positive and value at index(i,j) denotes the score the player gets if goal is scored at that location. The square region should be of size k*k. Find the square sub-matrix where the player should score a goal to get the maximum average score, where the average is calculated by finding the sum of elements in square matrix divided by number of elements in that square matrix. Second question was not a standard question. Again, it was given in the form of long story. Given, an array bike where element at index i, denotes the power of bike[i]. Also, an array of riders is given, where riders[i] denotes the riding capacity of the ith rider. Find how should the bikes be allocated to the riders, so that the product of bike[i]*rider[j] for every (bike,rider) pair should be greater than a given threshold value. We had to find all possible combinations. Sample Input: bike = [3,2,4] & rider = [7,3,5] threshold k= 8. Output: 4. Here, for 3 bikes and 3 riders, there can be 6 different combinations, but out of these, only 4 combinations will satisfy the given condition. (bike1,rider1), (bike2,rider2), (bike3,rider3) -> (3*7=21), (2*3=6), (4*5=20). Wrong combination as 2nd pair has product 6 which is less than 8. (bike1,rider1), (bike2,rider3), (bike3,rider2) -> (3*7=21), (2*5=10), (4*3=12). Valid combination as all pairs have product greater than 8. Similarly, 3 more valid combinations exist. I couldn’t solve both the questions due to the fact that only 30 mins were allotted for this section. Important tip: Based on constraints given, brute force solution can also prove to be sufficient to pass all test cases. Do try brute force solution. (2) Aptitude Questions: (45 mins). 12 Maths-based MCQ questions with +5 and -2 marking scheme were given. It had probability, permutation and combination, A.P., G.P., matrices, etc. somewhat like JEE mains. (3) HR Essay Section: (15 mins). 2 questions were given which were HR based, like describe your biggest achievement or questions like if you are working on a group project and one of your team members doesn’t complete his task on time, then what will be your reaction, and so on. (4) CS Fundamentals Section: (20 mins). 7 CS-Fundamentals related MCQ questions with +5 and -2 marking scheme. It had OS, OOPs, DBMS, CN, and a few debugging/output related questions. The questions were fairly easy or moderate, you only needed to worry about the time crunch. 16-08-2022 Interviews. All interviews are held on the same day. Note that the shortlisted students were announced 2 days prior to this day. We got the list on 14-08-2022. Out of all the students, 36 were selected for the interviews. The interviews were held offline, in the campus. Round 1: Technical Interview. My first interview lasted around 45 mins, while others had only about 30-35 mins of interviews. Interview began with the standard “Tell me about yourself” question. Make sure you prepare very well for this question. Based on your introduction, the interviewer might ask questions. I mentioned about my prior internship experience in my introduction, and the interviewer asked me to explain the internship project. Discussion went for about 5-10 mins, where I was questioned on tech stack and specific reasons why that tech stack was chosen. After that, he asked me few git & github questions related to branches, forking the repository, etc. Next, the interviewer jumped to DBMS. I had projects in which I used MongoDb. A lot of MongoDb questions were asked like why MongoDb? It’s comparison with RDBMS, the scalability of NoSQL databases. I was also asked to write a Mongo query (and I didn’t know it). So, I told the interviewer that I am not very comfortable with writing Mongo queries. NOTE: Mongo queries are generally not asked in interviews, so if you do not know something, very politely convey it to the interviewer. Next, he asked me some SQL questions like what are views? Advantages of view. I was asked about Indexing in DBMS and whether creating index is a DDL or DML operation. Then, interviewer asked to me write a query to create an index on some table which he gave me. I didn’t know the query to create index, so I couldn’t answer this question. Then, we moved to DSA questions. 1. Find middle node in a singly linked list. Pretty easy question. I straightaway gave both the brute force and optimal (slow and fast pointer approach) solution. I was also asked to write the code for the optimal solution. 2. Find kth node from the end of linked list. Again, a very standard question. The interviewer specifically mentioned to find it in only 1 pass. Gave the optimal solution for this question as well. 3. Largest subarray having sum zero. Told me to not mention brute force solution. So, I went on to give a TC-> O(N) and SC->O(N) solution using unordered map and also a sliding window approach which doesn’t require any additional space. Interviewer asked me to write the code for hashmap solution. While writing the code, always explain the code and “Think out loud”. Convey all your thoughts to the interviewer. I was also asked some conceptual questions regarding difference between array and list, what is arraylist and so on. I was not asked any questions related to OS and OOPs. Then, the interviewer asked if I had any questions for him. Always ask questions, so that they feel you are interested. This concluded round 1 and around 18-19 students out of 36, moved to the second round. Round 2: Technical Interview. This interview went very good for me and the interviewer was very friendly. It lasted for about 25 mins only. Initially, interviewer asked me which is my favourite subject/technology in Information Technology. I mentioned OOPs and OS. Important Tip: Whenever you are asked such open-ended questions, always try to drive the interview towards your comfort zone. Since I mentioned OOPs, we had a brief discussion on advantages of OOPs. Then, I was asked a question related to Encapsulation. I couldn’t answer the question as it was very tricky question, but then interviewer gave me a hint, and I immediately came up with the correct answer. Then, I was asked DBMS again. But, this time it was very easy. Different types of Joins and difference between INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN and RIGHT JOIN. The interviewer asked me a mathematical aptitude/puzzle question. Given, a machine which consists of only 2 types of balls. We can take out only 1 ball at a time. Find the maximum and minimum attempts to get 2 balls of same colour. Minimum = 2 attempts and Maximum= 3 attempts. Then, he asked me what if 3 balls of same colour are required, further I was asked to generalize it for n balls of same colour. Then, I was asked what if there are k types of balls in the machine and n balls of same colour are required. Ans: Maximum attempts = (n-1)*k + 1. This concluded my round 2 and I asked some questions to the interviewer regarding projects assigned to interns and tech stacks on which interns generally work at Goldman Sachs. Around 9-10 moved to round 3. We expected round 3 to be a HR round, as per past years experiences and process. But this time, round 3 was also technical round for everyone. Round 3: Technical Interview. Interviewer asked me how was I feeling after 2 interview rounds and was I feeling nervous. Then, asked me to explain a project and why did I choose to do that project. I was asked a question based on probability. There are 100 seats in an aircraft and you have booked one of the seats for yourself. 99 passengers are already seated at random places in the aircraft before you enter. What is the probability that the remaining 1 seat is your correct seat. After this, I was asked a DSA question. Given a binary array of 0’s and 1’s. Find the minimum number of swaps to accumulate all the 1’s together. (Not necessary that they are accumulated in front, or end or in middle of the array). This is a very good question on the application of fixed size sliding window. You can refer the question here. Then, I asked an interesting question. Given, 4 DBMS tables ( say A,B,C,D). All the tables are related to some table. Some deletions are to be performed on all tables. Devise an algorithm to find order in which deletions should happen, so that referential integrity constraint is not violated. For example above correct order could be: C,B,D,A or D,C,B,A. This is similar to Topological Sort in graphs. I was about to explain topo sort, but interviewer asked not to. She was satisfied with the fact that I could identify it to be topological sort. Then, we moved to DBMS question. I was asked to design a database table for student of a university where it should have personal information, courses information, department information and so on. I provided 2-3 tables, primary keys in those tables, foreign key in some tables. Later, interviewer pointed out certain flaws in database design. So, I applied normalization on the tables. After this, I was asked to write a query to find department name where more than 10 students are taking “C++” course on the database that I created. It was a complex query which required 3 table joins. I told the approach but couldn’t write the exact query with correct syntax. Interviewer asked me a typical HR question related to my thoughts on working together in a group project. Finally, interviewer asked me if I had any questions. We discussed the career path at Goldman Sachs and with this my round 3 ended. We were informed that there were only 3 rounds and no further rounds. HR round generally happens, but it did not happen this time. The interviews got over around 3 or 4PM and results were announced at 8PM on the same day. In the end, 8 students were selected for the internship and I was one of them. Resources which I followed: Data Structures & Algorithms: 450dsa (recommended) or striver’s list. Operating Systems: For good understanding of all the concepts, refer GateSmashers OS playlist and for OS notes refer this. Database Management Systems: Refer this for quick revision. SQL: Refer all the commands/clauses from tutorialspoint and practice on leetcode. For Low Level System Design, you can refer Soumyajit Bhattacharya’s playlist. OOPs: OOPs cheat sheet or javatpoint. NOTE: Read about vtables and vptrs. Many people miss out these imp concepts. Important Tip: Make a proper resume and do not lie in your resume. Mention only those projects/technologies in which you have contributed and have sound knowledge about. Be optimistic and trust yourself, you will eventually make it possible. ALL THE BEST :)
